text:
shilpa: Quick design question — should the saved-query preview show an estimated token/cost per model variant? cc @ben @tim
ben: I'm for it. Helps set expectations when users switch models in the UI.
erin: +1 but we should be careful about accuracy. sampling rates and prefix caching change costs.
tim: Agree we need a clear caveat. Could show a range: best/typical/worst.
shilpa: Thinking UX: small badge next to model name with a tooltip showing the estimate and the assumptions (sample rate, avg length).
ben: Also want a fast path: if route has pinned model, show the pinned estimate upfront. If not pinned, show both the default and the pinned suggestion.
erin: How do we compute estimates server-side? Do we reuse telemetry/route histograms or query the cost-estimator service?
ben: We can query the estimator sync on the server when generating the preview. It's cheap if we use cached per-route histograms.
tim: Important: saved queries can be shared org-wide. We need to surface quota impact so owners know who pays. Maybe a "quota impact" line that shows which team/account quota it would consume.
shilpa: UX idea: a compact "cost & quota" row in the saved-query modal. Example: "~12–18 tokens per call · uses Route A quota". Click for breakdown.
erin: That's nice. Also add a telemetry sampling toggle in the preview so users can opt-in to sample more for better estimates (with a consent prompt).
ben: Implementation note: Console currently calls /api/routes/:id/telemetry_hist to build graphs. We can extend that API to return an estimated_cost object. e.g.
```json
{
  "estimated_cost": {
    "model_variants": ["redwood-small","redwood-quant"],
    "per_call_tokens": {"min": 8, "avg": 12, "max": 22},
    "assumptions": "sample_rate=0.02,prefix_cache=enabled"
  }
}
```
shilpa: Nice. One open question — should saved-query scope (route-only vs org) affect the defaults? If a query is org-scoped, maybe default to conservative (higher) estimates to avoid surprises.
tim: Yes. Org-shared defaults should be conservative and show both per-route and org-wide previews.
erin: Another internal API debate: do we add a new field to the saved-query schema or compute estimates on-the-fly for the preview UI? Adding a field lets us snapshot estimates at save time (useful for audits), but will need migrations.
ben: I prefer compute-on-preview. Snapshots belong in the audit log rather than the saved-query object. We already store eval snapshots elsewhere.
shilpa: For rollouts: we can ship a UX-only change that calls the estimator but hides the feature behind a feature flag. Rollout plan: 10% teams -> 50% -> 100%. rollout-bot: canary started for feature=cost_preview, cohort=console-beta, 10%
erin: For telemetry sampling, let's add a non-blocking banner: "Improve estimates by opt-in sampling — low extra cost" with an opt-in button.
tim: Edge case: cached prefix length varies a lot by route; include "assumed prefix length" in tooltip so users understand variance.
shilpa: OK — next steps: Ben to prototype API extension, Tim to wire the small UI badge + tooltip, Erin to draft the opt-in copy, I'll create a short A/B plan for rollout and telemetry.
ben: I'll throw a draft PR for the API by EOD.
erin: I'll draft the text and put in #marketing-review after you, Shilpa.
shilpa: Thanks all. If anyone spots major holes say now, otherwise I'll create the JIRA and link the mockups. :thumbsup:
rollout-bot: feature flag cost_preview scheduled: start=2026-04-02T15:00:00Z cohorts=[console-beta]
